content:
As mathlib starts getting its adaptations for new Lean versions from downstream-lean4, the nightly-testing branch in mathlib4-nightly-testing will stop being updated.

The new bump-branch model

  • downstream-lean4 builds mathlib and other packages against each Lean nightly. Lean developers fix breakages there, in PRs created for downstream-labelled Lean PRs.
  • For bumps to the next toolchain version, bump/v4.X.Y branches (“bump branches”) will exist in mathlib4. The version number corresponds to the incoming toolchain version (the next version number to be released).
  • When downstream-lean4 has a green mathlib build, it merges master into the bump branch. It then opens a PR from downstream-lean4-fork-mathlib4 into the current bump/v4.X.Y with the accumulated adaptations. These PRs are referred to export PRs in the downstream-lean4 repo (and below).
  • These export PRs are merged with the standard review and merge process.
  • When the first release candidate corresponding to the v4.X.Y toolchain is released, the bump branch is merged into master without further review.

Contributing to a bump branch

For now, all changes reach bump/v4.X.0 through export PRs from downstream-lean4. A change merged into bump/* by any other route is reverted by the next export PR.

Note:

  • The PR diff contains only changes from the adaptations, the toolchain update and lake update.
  • Only one export PR is open at a time. No new adaptations reach the bump branch until that PR is merged or closed.

Contributors

  • PRs to master are unaffected. master reaches the bump branch automatically.
  • To help with adaptations, or to make a change that a reviewer asked for, open a PR in downstream-lean4. Ask @Joscha Mennicken for access. Do not open PRs against bump/*: the next export PR would revert them.
  • For Lean core changes, add the downstream label to the Lean PR and fix mathlib in the adaptation PR that downstream-lean4 creates.

Reviewers

  • Export PRs are expected to be reviewed up to mathlib's usual standards: in downstream-lean4, Lean developers (and bots) write the adaptations, and they get a light review there, aimed at keeping the build green; the export PR is their first full mathlib review. the bump branch will eventually be merged to master without further review

  • To request changes, comment on the export PR. The fix is made in downstream-lean4, and it reaches the bump branch in the next export PR. If the issue blocks the merge, the export PR should be closed, and after the next green build, downstream-lean4 opens a new one that includes the fix. Support for pushing modifications directly into the export PRs is planned.

Maintainers

  • Merge export PRs with bors r+, as usual
  • Consider that while one export PR is open, the bump branch does not get new adaptations
  • Only release managers and the downstream-lean4 bot can push to bump/* directly

In summary

  • If you pushed fixes for core changes to nightly-testing: make them in downstream-lean4 instead. Ask @Joscha Mennicken for access.
  • If you review or merge adaptations: see "Contributing to a bump" above.

Deprecations

The following will be retired:

  • The nightly-testing branch and its daily toolchain-bump and master-merge automation.
  • nightly-testing-green, new nightly-testing-YYYY-MM-DD tags, and the bump-branch reminders.
  • lean-pr-testing-* branches for adaptation PRs (these are already unused).

The mathlib4-nightly-testing repository will be archived when this new system is stable. If your project depends on mathlib's nightly-testing branch or tags: you can switch to the bump/* branch in mathlib4, but note that the name of this branch will change with each release. Please reach out if this is an issue, and we can consider maintaining a stable branch following the current bump branch.
Big shoutout to @Joscha Mennicken for the design and development of this new system, which allows us to simplify our CI automation and security model considerably
